content.value_statement: Shell scripts can hide portability, quoting, and reliability problems until production. This skill helps teams configure ShellCheck and apply practical linting workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains project-level .shellcheckrc settings for shell dialects, optional checks, and disabled warnings.
Shows how to run ShellCheck for POSIX shell, Bash projects, pre-commit hooks, and CI pipelines.
Maps common ShellCheck codes to practical fixes for quoting, exit checks, command substitution, and portability.
Provides guidance for suppressing specific warnings with comments and documented exclusions.
Describes output formats for local use, CI annotations, machine parsing, and quiet checks.
Covers simple performance patterns for checking many shell scripts.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not execute ShellCheck automatically.
It does not replace manual review for risky shell behavior or deployment scripts.
Examples must be adapted to each repository, shell dialect, and CI environment.
It does not verify installed ShellCheck versions or local package availability.

use_cases.title: Add Shell Linting to a Repository
use_cases.description: Create a project ShellCheck configuration and decide which warnings should block merges.

use_cases.title: Build CI Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Add ShellCheck checks to pull request workflows with consistent output for reviewers.

use_cases.title: Modernize Existing Shell Scripts
use_cases.description: Interpret common ShellCheck warnings and plan fixes for quoting, portability, and exit handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a basic ShellCheck configuration for Bash scripts in my repository. Explain each setting in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Review ShellCheck Warnings
prompt_templates.scenario: Fix warnings from an existing script review
prompt_templates.prompt: I have ShellCheck warnings for a shell script. Group them by risk, explain the cause, and suggest fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Enforcement
prompt_templates.scenario: Add repeatable checks to a pull request workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ShellCheck CI workflow for a repository with Bash and POSIX shell scripts. Include failure rules and exclusion guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Linting Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rollout for many scripts and teams
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged ShellCheck adoption plan for a large repository. Include baseline handling, suppression policy, ownership, and release gates.

output_examples.input: A team wants ShellCheck added to pull request checks for shell scripts.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a CI-focused plan with target shells, warning policy, reviewer output format, and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: A developer shares several ShellCheck warning codes from a legacy script.
output_examples.output: The skill explains what each warning means, ranks the likely impact, and proposes safer script changes.

output_examples.input: A maintainer needs to suppress a warning without hiding real issues.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends the narrowest suppression scope and asks for a documented reason near the affected line.

best_practices: Set the target shell explicitly so ShellCheck checks the correct language rules.
Document every disabled warning with a short reason and review it during maintenance.
Run ShellCheck both locally and in CI so issues are caught before merge.
anti_patterns: Disabling broad warning groups without a project reason.
Analyzing Bash-specific scripts as POSIX shell or POSIX scripts as Bash.
Treating ShellCheck output as a substitute for testing scripts in real environments.

faq.question: Does this skill run ShellCheck for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration and workflow guidance that you can apply in your own tools.

faq.question: Can it help with both Bash and POSIX shell?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to set the target shell and adjust rules for each dialect.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Will it tell me which warnings to ignore?
faq.answer: It explains suppression patterns, but each disabled warning should have a project-specific reason.

faq.question: Is it useful for CI setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for pull request workflows, pre-commit hooks, and build pipeline checks.

faq.question: Does ShellCheck find every shell script problem?
faq.answer: No. It finds many static issues, but runtime tests and manual review are still needed.
